scope: Read-only research and current app audit for high-school head-start learners and military-affiliated business-degree students. No academic awards, fee models or application files changed.

retrieval.note: Retained tool search/open/find results preserve observed extractions. Index crawl dates and tool retrieval are not origin HTTP response verification. Some primary .mil pages were blocked; those limits are explicit.

highSchool.quote: There are no age restrictions for Universal Learner Courses.
facts: College-level courses can be accessed before formal ASU admission, including by high-school learners.
Identity verification remains required. Learners under18 can begin with a birth certificate, but proctored exams require government-issued ID.
An admitted degree-seeking ASU student cannot use this open-access route; status exceptions are separately scoped.
High-school/NCAA treatment is the high school's decision. Do not promise simultaneous high-school credit merely from college credit.

highSchool.quote: with additional parental consent steps for learners under 18
facts: Families may enroll directly; how courses count toward homeschool high-school requirements follows applicable state guidelines.
College credit is recorded on the ASU transcript after eligible completion and optional purchase; institutional college credit and high-school treatment remain separate.
The course has $25 enrollment plus optional $400 credit purchase, and the credit-purchase choice lasts one year after finishing.
The provider describes separate high-school registration and additional parent-consent steps; follow that route instead of assuming an adult registration flow.

highSchool.quote: Sophia allows students as young as 13 to take college courses for future credits.
facts: This is the provider's stated access age, not a destination college's admission rule.
Sophia ACE-recommended learning is not itself institutional dual enrollment or an automatic high-school graduation credit.
Its article explicitly distinguishes state/institution age and grade requirements for dual enrollment.
uncertainties: The current general Terms of Use extraction did not establish a separate minor-consent policy. Do not invent a Sophia parental-consent requirement from a forum post.

highSchool.quote: Not be scheduled to graduate from high school prior to the completion of the dual enrollment course.
facts: Florida's program includes eligible public/private grade6–12 and home-education learners.
College readiness and local articulation requirements apply; the public guidance lists3.0 college-credit and2.0 career-credit GPA thresholds.
Home-education rules have specific statutory exceptions: do not apply a blanket high-school GPA requirement to a homeschool student.

highSchool.quote: Students who participate in dual enrollment programs are exempt from the payment of registration, tuition, and laboratory fees.
facts: The 2026 Florida statute provides a concrete tuition/registration/lab-fee exemption for eligible dual enrollment and separately addresses free instructional materials.
This is a state program with eligibility and articulation conditions, not a claim that every Florida teen's self-purchased ASU/Sophia course receives that funding.
For home education, documented home-education enrollment and a parent/student articulation agreement matter. Transportation may remain a student responsibility.

highSchool.quote: If you are completing college courses while in high school, you are considered a first-year student and not a transfer student.
facts: ASU defines transfer applicants by12or more transferable credits completed after high school.
Credit accumulation while in high school and first-year application status can coexist at ASU; do not promise the same rule at every school or guarantee scholarships.
The app should preserve high-school graduation timing and the target institution's applicant-classification rule, especially for campus-experience students.

highSchool.quote: students who must be 20 years old at the time of application
facts: YourPace admission age is a separate constraint from taking potentially useful outside courses earlier.
A high-school user should not receive an unqualified enroll-now YourPace action. A future-start plan needs the timing constraint.
highSchool.evidenceLevel: official indexed search excerpt; not a fresh open extraction in this packet

military.quote: Each school then decides how many credits they’ll accept.
facts: Army, Navy, Marines and Coast Guard follow the Joint Services Transcript route; Air Force and Space Force follow the Parchment route linked by VA.
ACE recommendations, original institutional credit and school-awarded degree placements must remain distinct.
Do not import every JST recommendation as earned degree credit or count overlapping civilian/military records twice.

military.quote: the tuition rate is $250 per credit hour
military.catalogScope: 2026–2027 Academic Year; undergraduate online certificates/associate/bachelor degrees
facts: The page lists active duty, Reserve/National Guard, eligible veterans/retirees, qualifying spouses and current Department of War employees.
Verification and institution-specific eligibility definitions apply. It excludes residential programs and requires qualifying veteran discharge status.
Military-child pricing is separately15% off regular full/part-time tuition for eligible new online students; it is not the spouse's $250 rate.
The page says benefits are not retroactive and the military-child discount cannot be combined with other discounts. Do not assume stacking.
Non-nursing undergraduate tuition applies to active duty, Air/Army National Guard, Reserve service members, their spouses/dependents, and DoD civil-service employees.
The page separates non-military/veteran tuition; veteran status alone does not establish this contracted military rate.
The military Edison Accelerate fee is$3468 if fewer than24 qualifying TESU bachelor's credits are earned (12for associate). Failure to graduate within15months can require another fee.
Books/materials are extra; graduation audit fee is$98; application$50 is currently waived for military/veteran learners. A per-credit discount alone is not a complete degree cost.

military.catalogScope: Public page explicitly labeled2025–2026; current2026–2027 rate not established by this page
facts: The course-based active-duty/spouse bachelor's table lists$250per credit.
A separate MyPath active-duty undergraduate row lists$250per credit up to12credits per24-week billing period; this is not the same unit structure as the course-based spouse rate.
Do not promise the course-based spouse discount for MyPath, infer all veteran eligibility, or convert this historical table into verified current-year MyPath pricing.
Current catalog and the student's approved tuition quote must resolve applicable year and modality before automatic price selection.

historicalRates.unit: per MyPath credit up to12per billing period

military.quote: Part-time is only available to service members utilizing Tuition Assistance.
facts: The part-time undergraduate option is6–11competency units; normal student and veteran GI-Bill enrollment are not automatically eligible for this option.
Tuition is prorated by attempted competency units, while resource/program fees remain full; federal financial aid is not available for this part-time option.
This is an enrollment/benefit-specific pricing mode, not a universal WGU military$250rate. The extracted pricing table loses program labels, so no business-specific rate is promoted.
Full-time acceleration may remain a better fit than choosing part-time solely because a military pricing mode exists.

military.quote: DANTES will only provide funding once for each CLEP exam subject.
facts: Eligibility depends on military/affiliation category; active/Reserve/Guard and limited spouse/civil-service cases are listed.
First-attempt subject funding, exam administration arrangements and remote proctoring must stay separate from credit acceptance.
Veterans may use qualifying GI Bill exam benefits; veteran status does not itself mean DANTES funds the attempt.
Retakes after a funded attempt are self-paid and have a waiting period. No blanket free-exams promise for dependents.

military.quote: pays your exam fee and remote proctoring fee for the first exam attempt per test title.
facts: The official College Board FAQ confirms fee and remote-proctor funding for the eligible first attempt.
Eligibility is indicated and checked during exam registration; proctored delivery remains proctored even when the charge is funded.

military.quote: Personnel not funded by DANTES include the following:
facts: Prometric's eligibility page differentiates actively serving members with required ID from retirees, discharged veterans and many spouse/dependent/civilian categories.
Coast Guard spouse and other specific exceptions must be evaluated separately; do not apply one blanket family rule across CLEP/DSST.
Remote DSST uses ProProctor with equipment requirements; Principles of Public Speaking is not available online.

military.quote: Guarantees CCAF AAS graduates need no more than 60 semester hours
facts: AU-ABC degree-specific articulation is a useful expansion source for qualifying CCAF graduates.
Category/program/prerequisite requirements must be checked; do not generalize to every CCAF record, every program at the partner school or all military learners.
military.evidenceLevel: official indexed discovery only; full page and exact business-program map not reviewed here

existingSupport.finding: Profile includes military status/branch/records/occupation, prior-credit estimate, state, budget and study preferences.
Actual service status adds the service-record step; dependents are not assumed to hold a service transcript.
Military onboarding distinguishes active, veteran, Reserve/Guard and family member, with appropriate records choices.
Existing record task selects CCAF for known Air/Space affiliation and JST otherwise; source links and inventory action exist.
A personal per-credit tuition quote can already represent a military discount.
Published estimates use sticker tuition, acknowledge discounts and explicitly describe TESU standard out-of-state assumptions.
Existing military-credit-jst-ccaf guide explains record collection, individual evaluation, overlap and benefit/curriculum separation.

verifiedGaps.finding: No high-school learner stage, age-band, graduation timing or dual-enrollment intent was found; HS-specific degree eligibility and funding cannot currently personalize recommendations.
One dependent/family category combines spouses and children even though verified institutional tuition rules differ.
Manual personal tuition quote exists, but no eligibility-scoped verified military price selection/total-fee comparison was found in these modules.
No dedicated HS dual-credit/head-start guide found. The generic before-enrollment article does not supply the state/provider/applicant-status distinctions.
Existing DANTES Zendesk JST source now redirects to a closed help center. Current accessible VA transcript guidance can replace that reference.

No explicit age/parent/children language found in the rendered terms/privacy text. A HS account flow needs a deliberate product/policy review rather than assuming the existing adult flow already covers it.

proposedAcceptanceCases.expected: Offer eligible local dual enrollment before self-funded provider purchases; keep college/HS applicability and destination business requirement separate; state and school agreement determine funding.
Show provider HS registration/consent and ID steps, transcript-purchase choice, state-defined HS treatment, and receiving school applicability. Do not promise universal dual credit.
Can plan appropriate outside courses; no enroll-now YourPace recommendation before verified minimum application age.
Collect original JST/CCAF and evaluate usable placements before buying duplicates; compare eligible military tuition including institution fees and funding rules.
Do not assign the same discount or DANTES funding to all. Retain separate affiliation and actual verified quote/benefit eligibility.
TA-dependent part-time option is separate from normal flat-rate full-time acceleration, with full fees and funding restrictions disclosed.

limitations: Read-only research/product audit only; no curricula, eligibility classifiers, price models, content pages or student records were changed.
Individual tuition and benefits eligibility remains subject to the relevant institution/agency decision; no credential, benefit or credit award is guaranteed.
